claims.text: Traditional Pt-based catalysts have high initial catalytic activity.
Traditional Pt-based catalysts degrade during long-term use.
High-entropy alloys can be formed by combining multiple elements in equimolar or near-equimolar ratios.
Pt can be alloyed in near-equimolar ratios with Ru, Ir, and possibly other elements to form the proposed high-entropy alloy catalyst.
Changing the elemental composition can tailor the catalyst's electronic structure.
Changing the elemental composition can tailor the catalyst's surface stability.
Potential cycling in acidic or alkaline electrochemical media commonly induces catalyst degradation.
The proposed alloy will form a stabilized, homogeneous high-entropy phase at its active surface.
Multielement interactions in the proposed Pt-Ru-Ir-containing alloy will modify the d-band center of Pt active sites.
Modification of the Pt d-band center will retain high HER activity.
Modification of the Pt d-band center will retain high HOR activity.
The complex, entropy-stabilized alloy structure will resist corrosion and degradation under harsh electrochemical conditions.
The proposed catalyst will have HER overpotential and exchange-current-density performance comparable to conventional Pt catalysts.
The proposed catalyst will have HOR overpotential and exchange-current-density performance comparable to conventional Pt catalysts.
The proposed catalyst will degrade more slowly than conventional Pt catalysts during long-term potential cycling in corrosive media.
Conventional Pt catalysts undergo performance losses because of corrosion and nanostructural degradation during prolonged operation.
The durability improvement depends on maintaining the high-entropy phase during operation.
Deviations from the intended elemental ratios could reduce the durability improvement.
Phase segregation could reduce the durability improvement.
